> Source: https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/general-instructions (retrieved 2026-11-23). Review articles, interviews, book reviews and IMPACT pamphlets are by invitation only on the same page. Submission is via ScholarOne (JOPE Manuscript Central).

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | No journal-specific AI clause on the instruction page (checked 2026-11-23); the OUP journals-wide policy applies, and per that policy a journal's own guidance prevails if it differs |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No prior-permission step in the OUP *journals* policy as read; disclosure is required |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | OUP journals policy (retrieved 2026-11-23): any generative-AI use must be disclosed, naming tool and version, how it was used and how the author directed and checked the output; disclosure goes in the cover letter and the Acknowledgements, plus Methods where AI was integral to the research; it is required at first submission and updated at each revision. Basic grammar correction and reference formatting are allowed without disclosure. Correction to the previous version of this entry: it cited the OUP *books* page, whose written-permission rule for AI-generated content is a books-division rule and was wrongly applied to this journal; leniency was 2 on that basis and is now 3. |
| **Source URL** | https://academic.oup.com/pages/for-authors/journals/preparing-and-submitting-your-manuscript/ai-principles-for-oxford-journals/policy-on-ai-use-and-disclosure-for-oxford-journals-authors |

## Format

Source for this section: https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/general-instructions (retrieved 2026-11-23).

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Original articles; review articles, interviews, book reviews and IMPACT pamphlets are by invitation only |
| **Word limit** | Preferably no more than 8,000 words; longer or shorter may be considered; over 8,000 needs a rationale in the cover letter. The page does not say whether references count |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Stated as a preference, with the cover-letter rationale route for longer pieces |
| **Abstract limit** | 250 words, no citations or abbreviations; six keywords |
| **Reference limit** | Not stated. Any readable style at submission, Oxford HUMSOC required before final acceptance; UK spelling except in quotations and references |
| **Supplementary material** | Allowed; submitted with the manuscript and cited in the text; published online only and not copyedited; appendices as PDF, data files zipped |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No numeric limit stated. Tables as separate editable files; each figure a separate file with alt text in the manuscript |

### Orientation

> Keyword counts below are from Crossref records for ISSN 0309-8249, articles dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 (515 journal articles; titles plus deposited abstracts, abstracts present for about 79% of them), retrieved 2026-11-23, matched locally. OpenAlex `works` queries were refused that day (daily budget used up), so Crossref was used instead; a keyword outside title/abstract is not counted, so these are lower bounds.

| Dimension | Assessment |
|-----------|------------|
| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Theoretical/conceptual dominates: "philosoph*" in 197 of 515 articles (38.3%), "conceptual" in 58 (11.3%), against "empirical" in 13 (2.5%) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | Few method terms at all: "interview" 13 (2.5%), "survey/questionnaire" 6 (1.2%), "qualitative" 3 (0.6%), "quantitative/statistical" 3 (0.6%) |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | Topic mix in OpenAlex spans religious education, political philosophy and medical ethics (table above); the about page names ethical, political, aesthetic and epistemological dimensions |

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** the about page (https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/about, retrieved 2026-11-23) says the journal publishes from a range of philosophical traditions, on basic philosophical questions about education and on critical analysis of current practice or policy. The previous pass's reading of 2024-2026 articles (Biesta reinterpretation, philosophy for children, difficult or postcolonial history, the IMPACT series) is retained as an earlier AI-research observation.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** conceptual-analytic philosophy; ideology critique; normative ethical and political argument; philosophical commentary on policy and practice (IMPACT series, by invitation); history of ideas and reinterpretation of theorists.

## Soft Metadata

### Epistemological & Political Leanings

- Scope statement: the about page lists "a range of philosophical traditions" and ideological forces shaping education as in scope (https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/about, retrieved 2026-11-23); no political or epistemological stance is stated on the pages read.
- Named thinkers in titles/abstracts of 515 articles, 2021-2026 (Crossref, retrieved 2026-11-23): Kant 27 (5.2%), Wittgenstein 21 (4.1%), Dewey 16 (3.1%), Heidegger 14 (2.7%), Arendt 10 (1.9%), Nietzsche 9 (1.7%), Foucault 6 (1.2%), Rancière 4 (0.8%), Marx 1 (0.2%); Biesta 11 (2.1%).
- Traditions/terms: "aristotle|virtue" 44 (8.5%), "liberal" 46 (8.9%, includes liberal-education uses), "pragmati*" 16 (3.1%), "phenomenolog*" 7 (1.4%), "critical theory|critical pedagogy" 7 (1.4%), "neoliberal" 12 (2.3%), "decoloni*/colonial" 30 (5.8%), "feminis*" 6 (1.2%).
- OpenAlex topics (spine, 2026-07-13): Political Philosophy and Ethics 419 articles, Pragmatism in Philosophy and Education 267, Wittgensteinian philosophy and applications 146.
- Reading of the counts: no single named thinker or school exceeds about 9% of articles, so the pattern is plural; analytic, Kantian/Aristotelian, pragmatist, continental and postcolonial strands all appear. This is a description of what is published, not of editors' politics.

### Framing Requirements

- Mandatory framing: no framing rule is stated on the instruction page; the about page defines scope as philosophical questions about education and critical analysis of practice or policy (https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/about, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Article types: original articles are the main route, preferably up to 8,000 words with a cover-letter rationale above that; review articles, interviews, book reviews and IMPACT pamphlets are invited only (https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/general-instructions, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Empirical papers are not excluded: Crossref titles/abstracts show interview or focus-group based articles (13 articles with "interview", 2.5%, 2021-2026), e.g. an empirical study of history teachers in francophone Belgium, DOI 10.1093/jopedu/qhag059.
- Consequence of ignoring the scope: no desk-reject statement exists on the pages read; SciRev shows n/a for immediate rejection (https://scirev.org/journal/journal-of-philosophy-of-education/, n=1).

### Methodological Preferences

Scoring rule: hits divided by 515 articles; 0 gives 0, under 1% gives 1, 1-5% gives 2, over 5% gives 3. Scores of 4-5 need an editorial statement and none was found. Source: Crossref titles/abstracts for ISSN 0309-8249, 2021-2026, retrieved 2026-11-23.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Theoretical / conceptual analysis | 3 | "conceptual" 58 articles (11.3%); "philosoph*" 197 articles (38.3%); capped at 3 by rule though clearly the dominant mode |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | "interview" 13 articles (2.5%); the term may also match interview-type items, which were not separated out |
| Survey / questionnaire | 2 | 6 articles (1.2%) |
| Case study | 1 | "case study" 3 articles (0.6%) |
| Ethnography | 1 | 5 articles (1.0% rounded; 0.97% exact) |
| Narrative inquiry | 2 | "narrative" 13 articles (2.5%) |
| Autoethnography | 0 | 0 articles in 515 |
| Quantitative / statistical | 1 | 3 articles (0.6%) |
| Historical / history of ideas | 3 | "historical or history" 43 articles (8.3%) |
| Policy / critical commentary | 2 | "critical theory or critical pedagogy" 7 articles (1.4%); the IMPACT pamphlet series is invitation-only (instruction page), so open-submission evidence is thin |

### Voice & Style

- Abstract: 250 words maximum, no citations or abbreviations, six keywords (https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/general-instructions, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- House style: any style at submission; Oxford HUMSOC and UK spelling before final acceptance; figures need alt text (same URL).
- Abstract sample for first-person use: Crossref abstracts deposited for 2021-2026 articles (denominator 409 articles, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Within that sample, "I" appears in 170 abstracts (42%), "we" in 140 (34%), "our" in 84 (21%), "my" in 32 (8%); "this article/paper/essay/study" in 289 (71%). First-person authorial voice is common, e.g. "In this paper, I will make an empirically based contribution" (DOI 10.1111/1467-9752.12545) and "We develop a Kantian approach" (DOI 10.1093/jopedu/qhag057).
- Recent openings sampled (DOIs): 10.1093/jopedu/qhag062, 10.1093/jopedu/qhag060, 10.1093/jopedu/qhag053 — two open with a general claim about education (qhag062, qhag060) and one names its topic directly ("This article attends to the negative emotion of disappointment", qhag053).

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

- Review model: double-anonymised (https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/general-instructions, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Editorial board page (https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/editorial-board, retrieved 2026-11-23): 29 named people (Executive Editor, 3 Co-Editors, a Book Reviews Editor, 2 Associate Editors, 8 Assistant Editors, 14 board members) across 10 countries; 15 list a UK institution, so UK affiliation is the plurality but not the majority.
- Executive Editor as listed: David Bakhurst, Queen's University, Canada (same page).
- Journal is associated with the Philosophy of Education Society of Great Britain (OpenAlex `societies` field and the about page).
- OpenAlex-derived topic mix of the journal's authors' work (spine, 2026-07-13): Religious Education and Schools 672, Education and Critical Thinking 522, Political Philosophy and Ethics 419 articles.
- Reviewer behaviour itself (tone, turnaround, expectations) is not observable from public pages; see the SciRev single review (n=1) under Review Cycle Time.

### Practical Concerns

- Originality and ethics: submissions must be original and not under consideration elsewhere; cases handled under COPE guidelines; third-party material needs copyright permission (https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/general-instructions, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- Conflicts of interest must be declared both in the submission system and in a statement in the manuscript (https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/general-instructions; the page is internally inconsistent on whether a statement is needed when there is nothing to declare).
- Preprints: allowed and do not block submission; update the preprint status and DOI after acceptance (https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/general-instructions).
- OA and charges: OA charge GBP 2,500 stated for 2023, waivers for qualifying developing-country authors (https://academic.oup.com/jope/pages/general-instructions); standard licence is free.
- AI: disclosure per OUP journals policy (URL in the AI Policy table).
- Anonymisation: double-anonymised, so title page with author details must be separable from the manuscript (instruction page).
- IRB/ethics-approval rule, data-availability statement, authorship criteria and independent-scholar rules: the instruction page states none of these (checked 2026-11-23).

## Strategic Notes

> Every statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Judgements about the journal's culture are not made because the evidence for them is absent.

### Hard Blockers

- A non-anonymised manuscript: the journal is double-anonymised (Peer Review table).
- Work already published or under consideration elsewhere (originality rule, Practical Concerns).
- Undisclosed generative-AI use beyond basic grammar or reference formatting (AI Policy table).

### Soft Tax

- Manuscripts over 8,000 words need a cover-letter rationale (Format table).
- After acceptance, references must be converted to Oxford HUMSOC with UK spelling, and figures need alt text (Voice & Style, Format).
- Timeline risk: the only SciRev report (n=1) records 12.0 months to first round and 28.0 months total; one data point, no reliable estimate (Review Cycle Time).

### Best Suited For

- Conceptual or normative philosophical argument about education: "conceptual" appears in 11.3% and "philosoph*" in 38.3% of 515 articles (Orientation, Methodological Preferences).
- Single-voice argumentative papers: first-person appears in 42% of sampled abstracts (Voice & Style).
- Papers engaging a named canon or a tradition: Kant, Wittgenstein, Dewey and Aristotelian/virtue themes each appear in 3-9% of articles (Epistemological Leanings).

### Not Recommended For

- A stand-alone quantitative study: "quantitative/statistical" appears in 0.6% of articles (Methodological Preferences); this is rarity, not a stated exclusion.
- Authors who need a guaranteed fast decision: the journal states no decision time (Review Cycle Time).
